page: Amazon Web Services c6gd.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by an AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor. This server features 8 physical cores and 8 vCPUs with a dedicated CPU allocation, operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz on the arm64 architecture. The CPU includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for AES cryptography, though it lacks AVX, AMX, and SHA_NI instruction sets. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB per core, and includes 474 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage. Network connectivity is rated at a 2 Gbps baseline bandwidth, and the instance runs on the Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates average multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 12133.14 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 5364.0. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by a Geekbench single-core score of 930.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1519.88. Memory bandwidth is average, reaching 473.11 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 116.89 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. The instance demonstrates average performance in database operations, with a Passmark database score of 5269.76 and 9.43 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-threaded compression and decompression tasks show weaker results, with bzip3 decompression single-threaded scoring in the bottom 10% at 6.93 GB/sec. LLM inference speeds are also limited, yielding 6.75 tokens/sec for a 7B model.

The qualitative cost efficiency of the c6gd.2xlarge is defined by its ARM-based architecture and the inclusion of local NVMe SSD storage, which reduces the need for external block storage for temporary data. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes it suitable for compute-heavy workloads that require fast local scratch space. Tradeoffs include lower single-threaded performance and the absence of x86-specific vector instructions. This instance is suited for workloads such as static web serving, software compilation, database operations, and multi-threaded processing tasks that can leverage the dedicated ARM cores and local NVMe storage.
